subject: Novus pilot: recommended inference stack & evaluation pack
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Grace Li <grace.li@novus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Novus pilot: recommended inference stack & evaluation pack

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the thoughtful questions. Per our conversation, I pulled together a concise decision kit to capture the recommended inference stack for the pilot, the key tradeoffs we saw in the live run, and the evaluation artifacts your engineers asked for. High-level summary first: 

- Recommended shortlist (balanced for quality -> latency -> cost):
  * Redwood-Stream-13B-fp16 — highest overall quality at 256+ token contexts; ~95th percentile latency ~120ms/token on our dedicated 8-GPU host; good for user-facing summarization flows.
  * Redwood-Chat-XL-8B-quant — lower cost, very good for constrained latency SLOs; quantization increases variance on long-context factuality tests.
  * Open-CDC-7B-q4_0 — cheapest; acceptable for internal routing/classification and embeddings-heavy paths, but expect lower hallucination resistance.

- Key tradeoffs: Redwood-Stream-13B yields best user experience but costs ~2.6x the per-token spend of the 8B quant variant; 7B-q4_0 can cut costs ~60% but requires stricter prompt/regression guarding.

What I attached / linked:
- novus_prompt_pack_v1.zip — canonical prompt templates we used in the demo (incl. few-shot examples and safety filters).
- benchmarks_novus_v1.csv — raw latency/cost/quality measurements from our replay of your demo dataset (256-token median tests + 1k random longer contexts).
- Drive links with interactive charts (benchmarks + prompt variants).

Suggested next steps:
1) Confirm target SLO (p50/p95 latency and quality thresholds) so we can recommend a concrete throughput plan.
2) If you want cost-first: we can prioritize Redwood-Chat-XL-8B-quant and run a quantization sensitivity pass. If quality-first: choose Redwood-Stream-13B-fp16 and we’ll scope a canary.
3) Commercial & procurement: Ben will share a PO-ready term sheet and pilot pricing options.
4) Ops/engineering: Mina can run a short op-runbook rehearsal (KV prewarm, batch sizing, cache TTLs) before you start the pilot.

If you’d like, we can schedule a focused 30-minute follow-up (technical) with your infra lead to walk the CSV benchmarks and iterate on the prompt variants. Are mornings next week (Tue/Wed) good?

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: novus_prompt_pack_v1.zip (zip, 2.1MB), benchmarks_novus_v1.csv (csv, 180KB)
From: Grace Li <grace.li@novus.ai>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novus.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novus pilot: recommended inference stack & evaluation pack

Thanks Evelyn — this is helpful and the write-up maps to what we discussed. A few quick clarifying questions before we lock next steps: 

1) For the 13B-fp16 numbers, can you share the p95 latency at 256 tokens (we need that for our UI SLOs)?
2) For the 8B-quant, what percent accuracy drop did you observe on the factual QA regression set versus fp16?
3) Procurement: we typically need SOC2 evidence and a short data-retention note for pilots to confirm compliance — can you share those?

Looping procurement for timing. If you can answer 1–3 above, we can confirm a preferred stack and timeline (we're targeting pilot kickoff in July).

— Grace
Grace Li | Head of Product, Novus.ai
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Grace Li <grace.li@novus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novus pilot: recommended inference stack & evaluation pack

Great questions — quick answers below and added detail for your procurement team: 

1) 13B-fp16 p95 at 256 tokens (our dedicated config used in the benchmark): 320ms per token (p95) — equivalent to ~82ms/token median during steady-state burst windows. We can dig into traces if you want per-request breakdowns.

2) 8B-quant accuracy on factual QA regression: ~4.2 percentage points drop vs fp16 on our Novus demo QA subset (mainly on long-context, multi-hop questions). For summarization and instruction-following, delta was smaller (~1.1–1.6 pts).

3) SOC2 + data retention: we have a SOC2 Type II report (PDF) and a short pilot data-retention statement: pilot logs retained 30 days by default; model outputs are retained per your preference (we recommend 30–90 days for initial debugging; we can opt for zero retention for sensitive flows). I will send the SOC2 doc via secure link — Ben, can you attach the compliance packet for procurement?

Operational notes / mitigations:
- Canary paths: route 20% traffic to 13B-fp16 for quality-critical endpoints, 80% to 8B-quant for cost control; automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant if latency spikes.
- Prompt/regression guards: recommend a small regression suite (50–100 prompts) for nightly runs — I put samples in the prompt pack.

Ben: can you drop the term sheet and a DocuSign for procurement? Mina: can you propose batch sizing and cache TTL defaults for Novus' traffic profile?

Thanks,
Evelyn
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Hi Grace / team — attaching a preliminary term sheet and pilot commercial options. Short summary: 

- Pilot package (4 weeks): flat monthly pilot seat + committed throughput block; optional overage priced per 1M token bucket.
- Pricing options:
  * Quality-path: Redwood-Stream-13B-fp16 — baseline pilot estimate $14k/week (depends on actual throughput).
  * Cost-path: Redwood-Chat-XL-8B-quant — baseline pilot estimate $5.2k/week.

Procurement: if the terms look good we can route a DocuSign envelope (link below) and provide SOC2/compliance packet on the signing page. Proposed milestone: sign by 2027-06-25, kickoff engineering alignment week of 2027-07-05.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/novus-term-sheet-01
Attachments: novus_term_sheet_v1.pdf (pdf, 45KB)

Would like to schedule a short call (20–30m) with your procurement and infra leads to confirm PO timing — are Thursday or Friday lunchtime PST available?

— Ben
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Novus pilot — ops checklist and regression concerns

Internal note (not for customer) — pulled from the demo and Grace's follow-ups: 

Action items before kickoff:
- Mina: run quantization-sensitivity experiment for 8B-quant on the 200-sample Novus QA subset and forward the delta report (target: <5pt drop). Deadline: 2027-06-16.
- Mina: recommend batch size defaults for canary (suggest 8–16 tokens/batch, dynamic batching based on 99th perc CPU/GPU queue length).
- Evelyn: assemble 50 prompt regression set from Novus prompt pack and wire into our nightly eval runner.
- Ben: prep SOC2 packet + push DocuSign envelope; confirm procurement timeline.

Risk notes: more aggressive quantization reduces cost but increases hallucination variance — for UX-critical flows we should default to fp16 or conservative quant profiles. Also ensure we have an early-warning automation for regression (30% QA drop or 50% increase in hallucination flags -> auto-revert canary).

I'll compile a short ops-runbook (2 pages) that Mina can send to Novus infra ahead of kickoff.

Evelyn
